newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian senator apologizes for Hitler comments.
newsitem.headline: Canadian senator apologizes for Hitler comments.

text.p: A Canadian senator apologized on Wednesday for suggesting Adolf Hitler should be a role model for policymakers when protecting citizens' safety was at stake.
The controversy began on Tuesday during a Senate committee hearing on legislation that would ban the use of a gasoline additive called MMT, which environmentalists have criticized as unsafe.
"If (Hitler) wasn't sure on MMT he would ban it outright," Joseph Landry, a Liberal senator from the province of New Brunswick, told the committee.
Widespread press coverage of Landry's remarks caused Canada's ruling Liberals acute embarrassment, and he apologized in a written statement.

"I made comments yesterday that were, upon reflection wrong and unacceptable," he said. "Citing Adolf Hitler to make a larger point was inappropriate -- even though I intended in no way to imply support for Hitler or any of his own poliices, which were evil and repugnant."
